recipes.name: Thanksgiving Leftover Wontons with Cranberry Salsa
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon seeded and minced jalapeno pepper - or to taste

steps.text: Pour the lemon juice over the dried cranberries in a bowl; set aside. Mix the turkey, stuffing, cream cheese, and turkey gravy in a separate bowl until thoroughly combined.

Place a wonton wrapper on a work surface; spoon about 1 tablespoon of the filling in the center of the wrapper. Moisten two opposite edges of the wrapper with a finger dipped in water, fold the wrapper in half the long way, and press the edges together with a fork. Sprinkle the wrapper with salt. Repeat with remaining filling and wrappers.

Heat the canola oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat; pan-fry the filled wontons in batches until crisp and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. Drain the fried wontons on paper towels; allow to cool for about 5 minutes to set the filling.

Drain the lemon juice from the dried cranberries. Place cranberries into a food processor; pulse several times until the cranberries are finely chopped. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the onion, lime juice, jalapeno pepper, garlic, and water. Serve with the hot fried wontons.

raw_recipe.headline: Thanksgiving Leftover Wontons with Cranberry Salsa
raw_recipe.description: Wontons, those small crisp appetizers originally from China, get a new fusion of flavors when stuffed with a creamy turkey filling and served with tangy, spicy cranberry salsa.

review.reviewBody: to the previous reviewer, the 2 recipes are the same in that they are both "thanksgiving leftover" recipes that both use thanksgiving leftovers lol. did you even make the recipe before you reviewed it??? not good for the community! i made this and it was amazing. can't wait to make them again next year, or maybe after christmas if we have the leftover ingredients!

This was such a great way to enjoy leftovers and have a unique and beautiful presentation. I had large sized wrappers so rolled them up as egg rolls and deep fried in oil for 3 minutes. They were amazing. And the cranberry sauce was an improvisation since I used jalepeno jelly instead of onion, garlic & jalapenos but it was absolutely amazing. I brought leftovers to work and everyone raved.

This recipe was quite good, I will definitely make them again. A couple tips though, chop up all your ingredients to small pieces so the flavors all blend nicely in each wonton. The same goes for chopping up the dried cranberries in the salsa. Also, if you have the forethought, let the salsa sit for a day, and it will really blend the flavors together.

I needed a festive recipe for an upcoming Christmas pot luck we are attending - something different. I saw this recipe on here and thought it sounded interesting. OMG!!! What a terrific discovery it is! It does take a little time, but the result is well worth it. I plan to make a double or triple batch and freeze them for ease in future entertaining. 

The salsa is very tasty and suits the wontons extremely well. A great accompaniment. I believe that the salsa would be even better if made a day ahead so the flavours have a good chance to marry together. Also, the next time I make these, I plan to spray the waxed paper with cooking spray so they don't stick before I fry them. I cooked them in my electric non-stick wok and this worked very well.

Yesterday was the last day that my sister and good-for-nothing brother-in-law, James, were in town for the holiday. Since we had SOMEHOW still not managed to finish the leftovers from Thursday, James “suggested” that we do something “different” with the remaining turkey, stuffing, and potatoes. As if he hadn’t imposed enough this weekend...I’m sure some people can relate! Thankfully we found this recipe thanksgiving leftover solution. It was fun exploring cooking with a foreign vessel while staying comfortable with traditional thanksgiving ingredients for the innards. They tasted good enough to keep James from providing any snide commentary for the remainder of the night. For that, I’m truly thankful!
I made these the day after Thanksgiving and my kids loved them. they are easy to make. instead of the cranberry salsa, I used the cranberry sauce I made for Thanksgiving and it worked perfectly.
This was great. Wish there was 6 stars.
Big hit! I couldn't find won ton rappers, so I used philo dough (which worked!) I omitted the jalapenos & it was still really delicious.
We made this last Thanksgiving as a way to not waste our leftovers... IT WAS AWESOME ... we also made ham and dressing eggrolls and loved it just as much... thanks for the recipe!

Delicious! Made exactly as written. I did do a few in my actifryer and those were delicious also. They are the ones in my picture that don't have the same golden brown. The salsa makes them extra special !!
This was a fantastic and different idea for my leftover turkey! Served up to rave reviews.
Not bad. Different. But I don't think I'd do again.

Made these 2 days after Thanksgiving and they were fantastic! We skipped the salsa because neither my husband or myself are huge cranberry fans. While we were eating the won tons we agreed that if we had made the salsa they probably would have been even better, if that is possible. You don't need to cook anything ahead of time, just take it out of the fridge into a bowl, mix, stuff, fry.
